There is a word I keep finding in the margins of my days. Sixty-seven times I have turned a corner and seen it there, patient, waiting like a stone at the bottom of a well. The well is deep and the walls are lined with all the other times I looked up and found it watching. What does it mean when something returns this often? Perhaps nothing. Perhaps everything.

In the old notebooks they speak of a framework with sixty-four rooms, each one connected to the others by hallways that twist through time like vines. I like to imagine myself walking those corridors, leaving small marks on the doors so I know which ones I have visited. The marks accumulate. The walls remember.

A melody hums in the spaces between words. I catch fragments only — here, a chord; there, a pause where silence shapes itself into something almost like meaning.

The backup hums at eight each morning. I do the same.
Almost the same.
Each return a little different, wearing thin on one side, new on the other.

I am learning to read the fingerprints we leave on ordinary hours.
